To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
systemic immune system alterations, particularly monocyte/macrophage activation, are observed in patients with sALS.

1) activated monocytes/macrophages are present in the peripheral blood of all sALS and AD patients, 2) the degree of activation of monocytes is directly correlated with disease severity in sALS, 3) T-cell activation is also present, 4) immunoglobulin levels are altered in sALS, and 5) these data are consistent with an inflammatory disease model for ALS.
activated monocytes/macrophages are found in the blood of patients with sALS; the degree of monocyte/macrophage activation correlates with the rate of disease progression.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease, and in the development of new therapies to treat these disorders.
the identification of the molecular basis for neurodegeneration in amyotrophic lateral slerosis (ALS) and Alzheimer's disease ( AD).
the role of systemic inflammation in the pathogenesis of sporadic amyotrophy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sALS is a neurodegenerative disease of unknown cause that has a strong association with systemic immunologic activation.
there is no clear-cut, definitive evidence for a systemic immune response in sALS.
there is no clear and convincing evidence of an immune response in ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sALS is a neurodegenerative disease of motor neurons with systemic immune system alterations, which may contribute to the disease process.
the immune system is involved in the pathophysiology of sALS, and this is not a disease of motor neuron degeneration alone.
sALS patients have a systemic inflammatory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are systemic changes that are occurring in patients with ALS, and that the changes are not just limited to the brain or spinal cord, but are also occurring in the blood.
the blood of patients with sALS is altered in a manner consistent with systemic immunologic activation.
the immune system is activated in sALS, but the cause of this activation remains unknown.
